core.title: Keep every referenced user/system flow sequence equal to its flow router route projection
core.given: A flow router route references a user/system flow, so the route has a projected sequence and the user/system flow has its own sequence.
core.when: Any referenced user/system flow sequence is checked at the confirmation phase (CONFIRM) — whether or not you edited the route or the user/system flow in this plan (editing either side is the common way to introduce a mismatch).
core.then: Make the referenced user/system flow sequence equal the flow router route projection step by step on step, intent, from, to and artifact.
prefer: Change the route and the referenced user/system flow sequence in the same plan step so they stay equal.
Compare step by step on all five fields (step, intent, from, to, artifact) for every referenced user/system flow before handing off to the confirmation phase, including untouched ones.
avoid: Matching only some fields (e.g. same steps but different artifact or from/to) and calling the sequences equivalent.
Editing only one side and leaving the other to drift.
Removing the user/system flow reference or editing the checker's expected projection only to get rid of the failure.
core.why: Guard coverage and the rest of the route reasoning are proven against the route-to-train projection, so a user/system flow that diverges from its route breaks that proof. The check is strict and blocks the confirmation phase.
evidence: The stack's projection-equivalence check passes for every flow router route that references a user/system flow.
Any failure pinpoints the flow router, route and user/system flow involved, the offending step and field, and the expected versus actual values; with zero such failures the rule is satisfied.
verification: A coherence check resolves each flow router route's user/system flow reference and compares the referenced user/system flow sequence with the route projection step by step on step, intent, from, to and artifact (the projection-equivalence term).

Checked in the confirmation phase (CONFIRM) and confirm-blocking; disposition strict, severity 4 — any mismatch on the five fields fails, including pre-existing mismatches not touched by the current change.

The check covers every user/system flow a flow router route references, edited or not; it does not cover user/system flows that no route references, and differences outside the five fields (e.g. prose or metadata) do not fail.
Each failure reports the flow router, route and user/system flow identifiers, the offending step and field, and the expected versus actual values.
An edit-triggered early warning (a diff observer resolving route-to-train references while either side is edited) is optional and not a prerequisite; absence of an edit does not exempt a sequence.

fires: The confirmation phase runs and any flow router route references a user/system flow whose sequence differs from the route projection in step order, intent, from, to or artifact — including mismatches that already existed and were not touched in this change.
A planner edits a flow router route so its projection now differs from the referenced user/system flow sequence.
A planner edits a user/system flow sequence that a flow router route references, without updating the route projection.
A new flow router route references an existing user/system flow whose sequence does not match the route projection.
doesNotFire: A user/system flow that no flow router route references.

A referenced user/system flow whose sequence already equals the route projection on step, intent, from, to and artifact (e.g. only prose/metadata differs); any mismatch on those five fields still fires regardless of what was edited.

profileRequirements.meaning: Which concrete plan-artifact kinds are the flow router spec (the subject) and the user/system flow specs its routes reference, so the check can recognize and resolve them in this stack.

neutralityNotes: The whole convention operates on plan-notation artifacts (flow router routes, user/system flow sequences, the route projection and its five fields), which are stack-independent by construction, so the core carries the obligation unchanged. The only Bun-specific content is the validator identity — the validator test id in evidence[0] and the validation family/template/variant registry ids in verifier_detail[1] — classified bunOnly, with the core describing the check generically. CONFIRM, confirm-blocking, strict disposition and severity 4 are per-rule verification facts kept in core:verification, not profile keys. One profile requirement (roles.plan_artifact.kinds) suffices to instantiate the file-kind fact for another stack; nothing was missing from the vocabulary, so proposedKeys is empty. The exact failure-field names (flow_router_id, route_id, user_system_flow_id, step, field, expected, actual) were kept in the core because they are domain-level, not stack-specific.
